title: The Power Broker #13: Drop Dead City

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: We spent a good chunk of last year on a special series breaking down The Power Broker by Robert Caro,
sentences.zh: 去年我们花了不少时间制作了一个特别系列，深入剖析了罗伯特·卡罗所著的《权力掮客》，

sentences.en: the incredible biography of New York City planner Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 那是一部关于纽约市规划师罗伯特·摩西的传奇传记。

sentences.en: The Power Broker is such a complete work, but the end of the book is not the end of the story.
sentences.zh: 《权力掮客》是一部非常完整的作品，但书的结尾并非故事的终点。

sentences.en: When The Power Broker was published in 1974, New York City was crumbling,
sentences.zh: 当《权力掮客》于1974年出版时，纽约市正处于崩溃边缘，

sentences.en: and its subtitle, Robert Moses and the Fall of New York, was widely accepted as truth.
sentences.zh: 而它的副标题《罗伯特·摩西与纽约的衰落》被广泛视为事实。

sentences.en: What Robert Caro didn't get to cover in the book was just one year later,
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·卡罗在书中没能涵盖的是，仅仅一年后，

sentences.en: the city went through a terrible financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 这座城市就经历了一场可怕的金融危机。

sentences.en: That crisis is the subject of a new documentary called Drop Dead City,
sentences.zh: 那场危机是一部名为《死城》的新纪录片的主题，

sentences.en: directed by Michael Rohatton and Peter YoSt.
sentences.zh: 由迈克尔·罗哈顿和彼得·约斯特执导。

sentences.en: The title is a reference to the infamous New York Daily News front page headline
sentences.zh: 片名源自《纽约每日新闻》那篇臭名昭著的头版头条，

sentences.en: published after then-President Gerald Ford made a speech saying that the federal government
sentences.zh: 发表于时任总统杰拉尔德·福特发表讲话称联邦政府

sentences.en: would not bail out New York.
sentences.zh: 不会救助纽约之后。

sentences.en: That headline, Ford to City, Drop Dead, is what most people remember about this whole saga,
sentences.zh: 那个标题“福特对纽约说：去死吧”，是大多数人对整段往事仅存的记忆，

sentences.en: if they know anything at all.
sentences.zh: 如果他们还记得什么的话。

sentences.en: But there's a whole lot more to the story.
sentences.zh: 但这个故事远不止于此。

sentences.en: Drop Dead City is excellent and compelling and does a great job explaining the situation.
sentences.zh: 《死城》非常出色且引人入胜，它很好地解释了当时的局势。

sentences.en: With interviews from nearly all the key players still around,
sentences.zh: 片中采访了几乎所有尚在人世的关键人物，

sentences.en: and some fantastic archival footage of 1970s New York streets and 1970s New York accents.
sentences.zh: 还有一些关于70年代纽约街头和70年代纽约口音的精彩档案影像。

sentences.en: It sort of feels like a coda slash next chapter to The Power Broker.
sentences.zh: 它感觉就像是《权力掮客》的尾声或下一章。

sentences.en: So I thought it'd be fun to break the movie down like we did with each chapter of The Power Broker,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，像我们之前拆解《权力掮客》每一章那样来拆解这部电影会很有趣，

sentences.en: and turn this into a special episode of the 99% Invisible Breakdown of The Power Broker.
sentences.zh: 并将其制作成《99%隐形》拆解《权力掮客》的特别节目。

sentences.en: Which means, of course, I had to call up my co-host, Elliot Kalin.
sentences.zh: 当然，这意味着我得叫上我的联合主持人埃利奥特·卡林。

sentences.en: So Elliot.
sentences.zh: 那么，埃利奥特。

sentences.en: Yes, Roman.
sentences.zh: 是的，罗曼。

sentences.en: When we last talked about The Power Broker, where did we leave our characters and where did we leave New York City?
sentences.zh: 当我们上次讨论《权力掮客》时，我们把书中的人物和纽约市留在了什么状态？

sentences.en: We left New York City doing great.
sentences.zh: 我们离开时，纽约市正处于鼎盛时期。

sentences.en: It was just doing fantastically well.
sentences.zh: 它当时发展得好极了。

sentences.en: Our old friend Robert Moses, the titular power broker, the master planner,
sentences.zh: 我们的老朋友罗伯特·摩西，那位名副其实的权力掮客、规划大师，

sentences.en: he had been finally pushed out of office.
sentences.zh: 他最终被赶下了台。

sentences.en: He was, as the final chapter of the book says, old and no longer in power.
sentences.zh: 正如书的最后一章所说，他老了，不再拥有权力。

sentences.en: He was frustrated by the lack of thankfulness and gratefulness that people were showing
sentences.zh: 他对自己为塑造这座城市所做的一切工作，

sentences.en: for all the work he had done to shape this city.
sentences.zh: 却没能得到人们的感激和认可感到沮丧。

sentences.en: Why weren't they grateful as the book ends?
sentences.zh: 为什么书结束时人们并不感激他？

sentences.en: One of the reasons maybe they were not grateful and why Robert Caro is so not grateful in the book
sentences.zh: 人们不感激他的原因之一，也是罗伯特·卡罗在书中如此不留情面的原因，

sentences.en: is because he leaves a New York behind that is doing financially very poorly.
sentences.zh: 是因为他留下的纽约在财政上极其糟糕。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is the New York that I think any of us, like myself, like I think you too, Roman,
sentences.zh: 这就是我认为我们任何一个人，像我一样，我想你也一样，罗曼，

sentences.en: any of us who love the New York movies of the 1970s knows pretty well, which is what I would call grimy New York.
sentences.zh: 任何热爱70年代纽约电影的人都非常熟悉的纽约，也就是我所说的“肮脏的纽约”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The New York of there's garbage all over the streets, there's drug addicts everywhere, the subways don't work.
sentences.zh: 那个街头到处是垃圾、到处是瘾君子、地铁瘫痪的纽约。

sentences.en: This was a New York that was desperately struggling to provide the level of service to its citizens
sentences.zh: 那是一个拼命挣扎着为市民提供服务，

sentences.en: that it had taken for granted, that it would be able to provide.
sentences.zh: 而这些服务曾被视为理所当然的纽约。

sentences.en: And you can't blame all of this for Robert Moses, but it's so tempting to just because we spent so much time talking about him.
sentences.zh: 你不能把这一切都归咎于罗伯特·摩西，但因为我们花了这么多时间谈论他，这太诱人了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And this brings us to what we're discussing today, at least the piece of pop culture that is, you know,
sentences.zh: 这就引出了我们今天讨论的主题，至少是作为流行文化的那一部分，你知道，

sentences.en: centering our discussion, which is this movie called Drop Dead City, which is a documentary about the 1970s New York financial crisis
sentences.zh: 我们讨论的核心是这部名为《死城》的电影，这是一部关于70年代纽约金融危机

sentences.en: and the sort of austerity that followed.
sentences.zh: 以及随之而来的紧缩政策的纪录片。

sentences.en: And it really sets a scene of the fall of New York in the subtitle of The Power Broker.
sentences.zh: 它确实为《权力掮客》副标题中的“纽约的衰落”定下了基调。

sentences.en: Like it really shows you what Robert Carroll was getting at and why he was so mad.
sentences.zh: 它真的向你展示了罗伯特·卡罗想要表达的内容，以及他为什么那么愤怒。

sentences.en: And anytime we've ever talked to him where we go, maybe, you know, like in retrospect, you think back, maybe a little harsh on Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 每当我们和他交谈时，我们都会说，也许，你知道，回顾过去，你对罗伯特·摩西是不是有点太苛刻了。

sentences.en: He's like, no, I was, if nothing, I went easy on him.
sentences.zh: 他会说，不，我当时，如果说有什么的话，我已经对他很客气了。

sentences.en: I was too nice.
sentences.zh: 我对他太好了。

sentences.en: I was too nice to him.
sentences.zh: 我对他太好了。

sentences.en: One of the things that strikes me so much about this movie, there's so much great footage in it of just street scenes of New York,
sentences.zh: 这部电影最让我震撼的一点是，里面有大量关于纽约街头场景的精彩镜头，

sentences.en: what New York looked at the time.
sentences.zh: 展示了当时的纽约是什么样子。

sentences.en: And you look at it and you're like, oh, this New York looks like it is crumbling, that it's physically falling apart.
sentences.zh: 看着那些画面，你会觉得，哦，这个纽约看起来正在崩溃，它在物理上分崩离析。

sentences.en: And even the nice parts of the city that you see, because there's lots of scenes of union leaders and bank executives showing up in their cars at meetings.
sentences.zh: 即使是城市里看起来不错的地方，因为片中有很多工会领袖和银行高管开车去开会的场景，

sentences.en: Even the nice parts look sickly.
sentences.zh: 连那些不错的地方看起来也病恹恹的。

sentences.en: Like there's this kind of like horrible sickly 70s feel to it.
sentences.zh: 就像有一种可怕的、病态的70年代氛围。

sentences.en: Fluorescent lighting, yeah.
sentences.zh: 荧光灯，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: It's like if this is the everything's orange and brown, I kind of like it.
sentences.zh: 就像如果这就是一切都是橙色和棕色的世界，我其实还挺喜欢的。

sentences.en: But all these guys who are in suits have very long hair.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些穿西装的家伙都留着长发。

sentences.en: You're just like, I need Sidney Lumet to get the fuck out of here and stop lighting this place because everyone looks horrible.
sentences.zh: 你只会觉得，我需要西德尼·吕美特赶紧滚蛋，别再给这地方打光了，因为每个人看起来都糟透了。

sentences.en: But you understand while you're watching it, oh, if this is the New York that Robert Carroll is living in while he's finishing The Power Broker because he started it, you know,
sentences.zh: 但你在观看时会明白，哦，如果这就是罗伯特·卡罗在完成《权力掮客》时所处的纽约，因为他开始写这本书是在，你知道，

sentences.en: eight years earlier.
sentences.zh: 八年前。

sentences.en: If this is New York he's living in while he's finishing it, no wonder he's mad.
sentences.zh: 如果这就是他完成书时所处的纽约，难怪他会生气。

sentences.en: No wonder it's the fall of New York in the subtitle because New York looks like it is in decay.
sentences.zh: 难怪副标题是“纽约的衰落”，因为纽约看起来确实在腐烂。

sentences.en: You know, it looks just terrible.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它看起来太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And so that's the first striking thing in this movie, the sort of visuals of that.
sentences.zh: 所以这是这部电影给人的第一个震撼点，那种视觉效果。

sentences.en: The other striking thing that I love about this movie is the New York accents are just out of control.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这部电影的另一个震撼点是，里面的纽约口音简直太绝了。

sentences.en: We have flattened culture by I think social media and stuff of like regional accents have really fallen away,
sentences.zh: 我认为社交媒体等因素已经让文化趋于平庸，区域口音真的消失了，

sentences.en: especially the sort of quintessential New York accent has really like diminished.
sentences.zh: 尤其是那种典型的纽约口音真的减弱了。

sentences.en: Because kids are interviewed on the street talking about Mayor Abe Bean.
sentences.zh: 因为片中街头采访的孩子们在谈论市长亚伯·比姆。

sentences.en: I think that's not fair.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这不公平。

sentences.en: Why should people get laid off?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们要被解雇？

sentences.en: Well, the mayor says there isn't enough money to pay him.
sentences.zh: 嗯，市长说没有足够的钱付工资。

sentences.en: Well, I don't care what he says.
sentences.zh: 我才不管他说什么。

sentences.en: He's just a dumb old bum.
sentences.zh: 他只是个愚蠢的老流浪汉。

sentences.en: It's just like, it's so fantastic.
sentences.zh: 这简直太棒了。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它。

sentences.en: And the movie immediately delights with the visuals and the sound of New York City in 1975.
sentences.zh: 这部电影通过1975年纽约市的视觉和声音，立刻让人感到愉悦。

sentences.en: It's spectacular.
sentences.zh: 太壮观了。

sentences.en: I feel the same way because as much as I was saying, oh, it's crumbling, the city is falling apart, there's still something so enticing about it.
sentences.zh: 我有同感，因为尽管我一直在说，哦，它在崩溃，城市在分崩离析，但它仍然有一种如此吸引人的东西。

sentences.en: And maybe it's just the young punk in me that refuses to die all the way knowing that there's going to be all these amazing things that come out of this decay.
sentences.zh: 也许只是我内心那个拒绝彻底死去的年轻朋克，知道从这种衰败中会诞生出所有这些了不起的东西。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But perhaps it's like you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 但也许就像你说的。

sentences.en: It's that the accents are so strong, the personality of the people in the city and the personality of the city is so strong.
sentences.zh: 是因为口音太浓郁了，城市里人们的个性和这座城市本身的个性太强烈了。

sentences.en: Whereas New York, as much as I love it, it's still the greatest city in the world and always will be.
sentences.zh: 虽然我热爱纽约，它仍然是世界上最伟大的城市，永远都是。

sentences.en: It's a city that does not feel as distinctly New York as it once was.
sentences.zh: 但它现在感觉不像以前那样具有独特的“纽约味”了。

sentences.en: And the saddest aspect of the movie is that New York at the time is having trouble taking care of its citizens.
sentences.zh: 这部电影最令人悲伤的一面是，当时的纽约在照顾市民方面遇到了困难。

sentences.en: It's having trouble living day to day because it's running out of money and it's living on debt.
sentences.zh: 它难以维持日常运转，因为它没钱了，只能靠举债度日。

sentences.en: But the second saddest part of it is this undercurrent of, yeah, things were bad, but there was still something New York about this place.
sentences.zh: 但第二悲伤的部分是这种潜流，是的，情况很糟糕，但这个地方仍然有一些属于纽约的东西。

sentences.en: And the process of the austerity that was brought in,
sentences.zh: 而引入紧缩政策的过程，

sentences.en: the money that was brought in to get New York back on its feet financially inevitably has that flattening effect that you're talking about where New York stops being itself and becomes instead the global capital of finance,
sentences.zh: 为了让纽约在财政上重新站稳脚跟而注入的资金，不可避免地产生了你所说的那种平庸化效应，纽约不再是它自己，而是变成了全球金融之都，

sentences.en: you know, which is not a not as fun a place to be.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那可不是一个那么有趣的地方。

sentences.en: Well, right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没错。

sentences.en: And that's a big theme of this movie and this sort of like any sort of history of this time period is, you know,
sentences.zh: 这是这部电影的一个大主题，也是这一时期任何历史的共同点，你知道，

sentences.en: this was the last vestige of New York City being a working class city where most people were part of a union.
sentences.zh: 这是纽约市作为工人阶级城市的最后遗迹，大多数人都是工会成员。

sentences.en: There was a large, you know, like infrastructure of workers in the city.
sentences.zh: 城市里有庞大的，你知道，工人基础设施。

sentences.en: They could afford maybe not to live in Manhattan, but they could buy a house in Brooklyn or Queens.
sentences.zh: 他们可能买不起曼哈顿的房子，但他们能在布鲁克林或皇后区买房。

sentences.en: And this is hitting at this moment where this is breaking because there's all these city services that are being offered and the unions are quite powerful and they've made a good life for the people who are underneath the unions.
sentences.zh: 而这一时刻正面临崩溃，因为城市提供的所有这些服务，工会力量非常强大，他们为工会下属的人们创造了美好的生活。

sentences.en: But many forces are making it so like the economic centers of the city are leaving.
sentences.zh: 但许多力量正在使其瓦解，比如城市的经济中心正在离开。

sentences.en: So like factories are leaving the city.
sentences.zh: 工厂正在离开这座城市。

sentences.en: They're no longer in place.
sentences.zh: 它们不再存在了。

sentences.en: White people are leaving the city.
sentences.zh: 白人正在离开这座城市。

sentences.en: They're no longer there as a tax base.
sentences.zh: 他们不再是税基了。

sentences.en: And city services are keeping up.
sentences.zh: 而城市服务却在跟进。

sentences.en: And this is further complicating the financial problems of the city.
sentences.zh: 这进一步加剧了城市的财政问题。

sentences.en: But it turns out that the financial problems have been a long time coming, but nobody knew about them because the city kept horrible books.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，财政问题由来已久，只是没人知道，因为这座城市的账目做得太烂了。

sentences.en: They didn't have an accounting system that made any sense.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没有一套合理的会计系统。

sentences.en: It was chaotic.
sentences.zh: 那是一团乱麻。

sentences.en: Everybody had stuff in drawers.
sentences.zh: 每个人都把东西塞在抽屉里。

sentences.en: Everybody had buried and buried stuff.
sentences.zh: 每个人都把事情掩盖起来。

sentences.en: And there's got to be a good end to some of this.
sentences.zh: 这其中总得有个好的结局吧。

sentences.en: There were no f***ing books.
sentences.zh: 根本就没有他妈的账本。

sentences.en: I've mentioned before on the Power Roker podcast, my favorite movie is The Taken, Pelham, 123, the 1974 edition.
sentences.zh: 我之前在《权力掮客》播客中提到过，我最喜欢的电影是1974年版的《地铁惊魂》。

sentences.en: And I love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢它了。

sentences.en: But the whole time I'm watching it, loving it, I'm like, I'm so glad I don't have to live in this city and deal with these people who are in it.
sentences.zh: 但看电影的时候，我一边喜欢它，一边想，我真庆幸自己不必住在这个城市，也不必和里面这些人打交道。

sentences.en: Because all of these very kind of like quaint, fun, abrasive New York types are probably not the easiest people to work with or deal with on a day-to-day basis.
sentences.zh: 因为所有这些古怪、有趣、刻薄的纽约人，可能不是那种在日常生活中容易共事或相处的人。

sentences.en: And an example of that is that the bookkeeping of the city – this is a city that's been around for hundreds of years by this point.
sentences.zh: 一个例子就是城市的记账方式——这可是一个已经存在了几百年的城市。

sentences.en: And the bookkeeping of the city is nonexistent.
sentences.zh: 但城市的记账方式根本不存在。

sentences.en: It's basically run the way that like a guy just out of college does his taxes where he just has a bunch of like crumpled receipts and maybe he printed out the form to pay his taxes.
sentences.zh: 它基本上就是像一个刚毕业的大学生报税的方式，只有一堆揉皱的收据，可能还打印了一张报税表。

sentences.en: And it's just astonishing the way that the city has done such a good – I guess it's a real tribute to the New York spirit that's done such a good job of surviving when nobody knows how much money is being spent on anything or how much money the city has at any given point.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，这座城市竟然做得这么好——我想这真是纽约精神的写照，在没人知道任何东西花了多少钱，或者城市在任何给定时刻有多少钱的情况下，竟然还能生存下来。

sentences.en: And you can't look at a ledger and say, here's what the budget is, here's what our debt is, here's what the deficit is, here's how much we're paying each of these departments.
sentences.zh: 你无法查看账本并说，预算是多少，债务是多少，赤字是多少，我们给每个部门付了多少钱。

sentences.en: Instead, it's just various rogue numbers floating around in different people's heads and on different scraps of paper.
sentences.zh: 相反，只有各种流氓数字在不同人的脑子里和不同的纸条上飘来飘去。

sentences.en: And one of the amazing things about this is that the mayor who this is going to fall on the hardest, Abe Beam, he was the comptroller beforehand.
sentences.zh: 其中最令人惊奇的事情之一是，最倒霉的市长亚伯·比姆，他之前是审计长。

sentences.en: So he's partly responsible for how disorganized the system is because he was the guy who was keeping the city afloat using scraps of paper, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以他要对系统的混乱负部分责任，因为他就是那个用纸条维持城市运转的人，你知道。

sentences.en: Well, what he's a victim of here, why he's sort of caught holding the bag at the end, is there was a way of doing things for a couple hundred years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他在这里的受害者身份，为什么他最后成了背锅侠，是因为这种做事方式已经持续了几百年。

sentences.en: And it was fine because the city was so massive that the cash flow was so great that it could mask what side of the ledger any sort of, you know, transaction was on.
sentences.zh: 而且这没问题，因为城市太庞大了，现金流太充裕了，以至于可以掩盖任何交易在账目的哪一边。

sentences.en: Like if there's money flowing through, it doesn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 就像如果有钱流进来，其实并不重要。

sentences.en: You're kind of constantly borrowing.
sentences.zh: 你一直在借钱。

sentences.en: You're constantly in debt.
sentences.zh: 你一直负债累累。

sentences.en: But you're always giving money out.
sentences.zh: 但你总是在往外发钱。

sentences.en: And everyone kind of gets paid somehow.
sentences.zh: 每个人总能以某种方式拿到工资。

sentences.en: And it kind of works.
sentences.zh: 它就这样运作着。

sentences.en: Especially at the end of World War II when New York is a major manufacturing center, it's the place people from all over the world are coming to to do work.
sentences.zh: 特别是在二战结束时，纽约是一个主要的制造业中心，是世界各地的人们前来工作的地方。

sentences.en: And it's just a – it's flush with money.
sentences.zh: 它简直是——钱多得花不完。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's just money flowing through it.
sentences.zh: 是的，钱就在里面流转。

sentences.en: So it's like, oh, the bill on the sanitation came through.
sentences.zh: 所以就像，哦，环卫部门的账单来了。

sentences.en: Well, here's 10 bucks I found in a desk drawer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是我在抽屉里找到的10块钱。

sentences.en: You can use that.
sentences.zh: 你可以用那个。

sentences.en: Oh, great, great.
sentences.zh: 哦，太好了，太好了。

sentences.en: We got to pay these teachers.
sentences.zh: 我们得付老师工资。

sentences.en: Hold on a second.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: Yeah, here's some money over here.
sentences.zh: 是的，这儿有些钱。

sentences.en: It's all very – it's very slushy.
sentences.zh: 这一切都非常——非常混乱。

sentences.en: It's all very slushy the way they handle it.
sentences.zh: 他们处理账目的方式简直是一团糟。

sentences.en: Slushy is very much the way it is.
sentences.zh: “烂泥”的状态大抵就是如此。

sentences.en: And so this habit of borrowing money, this has been a long time coming.
sentences.zh: 所以这种借钱的习惯，由来已久。

sentences.en: In fact, it's possible that they were kind of taught this by Robert Moses, like in terms of like making bonds available, funding things, and then paying them back.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们很可能是从罗伯特·摩西那里学来的，比如通过发行债券、筹集资金，然后再偿还。

sentences.en: So from the Power Broker book, where do you place the beginning of the sort of borrowing money for services that seems to be the sort of the thing that starts the downfall here?
sentences.zh: 那么，从《权力掮客》这本书来看，你认为这种为了公共服务而借钱的行为，是从哪里开始的？这似乎就是导致后来衰败的开端。

sentences.en: So I think you're right that Robert Moses, his big policy is you issue a bond to pay for a big infrastructure improvement, for a bridge, for a tunnel.
sentences.zh: 我认为你说得对，罗伯特·摩西的主要策略就是发行债券，来支付大型基础设施的改善费用，比如桥梁、隧道。

sentences.en: The tolls pay you back, and you pay the bondholders, and it becomes a constant, eternal, perpetual money machine.
sentences.zh: 过路费用来偿还你，你再支付给债券持有人，这就变成了一台永不停歇、永恒运转的印钞机。

sentences.en: And when Mayor Wagner is mayor of New York, there's a funding shortfall.
sentences.zh: 当罗伯特·瓦格纳担任纽约市长时，出现了资金缺口。

sentences.en: And for really the first major time, the city itself is now issuing a bond.
sentences.zh: 这是纽约市历史上第一次真正意义上的大规模举债。

sentences.en: It's now borrowing money in order to pay not just a big capital improvement bill, not a new thing like a bridge or a tunnel or a stadium or an aquarium or something like that.
sentences.zh: 它现在借钱不仅仅是为了支付大型资本改善项目，不再是像桥梁、隧道、体育场或水族馆之类的新建项目。

sentences.en: That's a one-time fee that will pay itself off.
sentences.zh: 那是一次性费用，最终会收回成本。

sentences.en: But they're borrowing money for the first time to cover the day-to-day expenses of the city.
sentences.zh: 但他们第一次借钱是为了应付城市的日常开支。

sentences.en: And this is seen as an out-of-the-ordinary thing.
sentences.zh: 这被视为一种非同寻常的行为。

sentences.en: We are not going to make a habit out of this.
sentences.zh: 我们不会让这种事成为习惯。

sentences.en: The tax revenues are going to come in.
sentences.zh: 税收收入会进账的。

sentences.en: We're going to pay it off.
sentences.zh: 我们会还清的。

sentences.en: We're going to balance these books on the sheets of paper in Abe Beam's pocket.
sentences.zh: 我们会平衡好亚伯·比姆口袋里那张纸上的账目。

sentences.en: And then when Mayor John Lindsay comes in after Wagner, it becomes much more of a problem for New York to meet those bills and becomes a regular thing to borrow money.
sentences.zh: 后来，当约翰·林赛接替瓦格纳担任市长时，纽约要支付这些账单就变得更加困难，借钱也成了家常便饭。

sentences.en: Now suddenly New York is living on its credit card the way that so many average everyday Americans do where it is living on borrowed money,
sentences.zh: 现在，纽约突然像许多普通美国人一样靠信用卡生活，靠借来的钱度日，

sentences.en: and it can never fully pay off that money.
sentences.zh: 而且它永远无法完全还清这笔钱。

sentences.en: And so by the time Abe Beam is mayor, that has caught up with New York.
sentences.zh: 所以等到亚伯·比姆当市长时，这个问题已经让纽约陷入了困境。

sentences.en: It can no longer continue to borrow money without paying off the money it owes,
sentences.zh: 它再也无法在不偿还债务的情况下继续借钱了，

sentences.en: and it's paying so much to service the debt that a larger and larger portion of its budget is being used just to pay off previous debt that it borrowed.
sentences.zh: 而且它支付利息的成本太高，预算中越来越大的一部分仅仅被用来偿还之前借下的债务。

sentences.en: And they keep saying, well, the tax revenues will come in.
sentences.zh: 他们一直说，税收收入会进来的。

sentences.en: Well, we're going to have a flush time, and then we'll pay everything off, which is – it's like classic Vegas gambler addiction talk.
sentences.zh: 我们会迎来一段富足时期，然后把一切都还清，这简直是典型的拉斯维加斯赌徒式的说辞。

sentences.en: It was like Heat with Robert De Niro basically where it's like just one last big score.
sentences.zh: 就像罗伯特·德尼罗主演的电影《盗火线》，基本上就是说“再干最后一票大的”。

sentences.en: Then we'll be done.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就收手。

sentences.en: That's Val Cummer.
sentences.zh: 那是瓦尔·卡默说的。

sentences.en: Then we'll be done.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就收手。

sentences.en: Just one last score.
sentences.zh: 就再干最后一票。

sentences.en: But everything goes terribly.
sentences.zh: 但一切都搞砸了。

sentences.en: Spoiler for the movie Heat.
sentences.zh: 剧透一下电影《盗火线》。

sentences.en: The big heist doesn't go off the way they want it to, you know?
sentences.zh: 那场大劫案并没有按他们预想的那样进行，你懂的？

sentences.en: And this is also reflected in the state budget as well.
sentences.zh: 这种情况也反映在州预算中。

sentences.en: Nelson Rockefeller, the sort of northeast liberal Republican, which doesn't really exist anymore, was also quite a spender, liked to provide services, was, you know,
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊·洛克菲勒，那种现在已经不存在的东北部自由派共和党人，也是个大手大脚的人，喜欢提供公共服务，他是个，你知道的，

sentences.en: I think a man with a good moral compass.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他是一个有良好道德准则的人。

sentences.en: I have no objections to him greatly.
sentences.zh: 我对他没什么太大的意见。

sentences.en: You know, but like – but also was a spender and took a lot of pride in the services that were provided to New Yorkers through the state government.
sentences.zh: 你知道，但他也是个花钱大手大脚的人，并为通过州政府为纽约人提供的服务感到自豪。

sentences.en: So all of this, this was just the habit of the time and the habit of New York.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切，这只是当时的习惯，也是纽约的习惯。

sentences.en: Not just in New York.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是在纽约。

sentences.en: This was city, state, and federal.
sentences.zh: 这是城市、州和联邦层面的共同习惯。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because this is the era of the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 因为这是20世纪60年代的时代背景。

sentences.en: It's the time of the great society.
sentences.zh: 那是“伟大社会”的时代。

sentences.en: We are post-World War II, and America is saying, how can we, the most powerful country in the world, have poor people?
sentences.zh: 我们处于二战后，美国在问：作为世界上最强大的国家，我们怎么能还有穷人？

sentences.en: How can we have hungry people?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么能还有挨饿的人？

sentences.en: We have to take care of everybody.
sentences.zh: 我们必须照顾每一个人。

sentences.en: And it is the best of intentions, and their ambitions become larger and larger about how to do this, and unfortunately, economic forces change, time changes,
sentences.zh: 这是出于最好的初衷，他们对于如何实现这一目标的野心也越来越大，但不幸的是，经济力量在变化，时代在变，

sentences.en: and suddenly they're not as flush with money.
sentences.zh: 突然间，他们不再那么财大气粗了。

sentences.en: And it's very hard to put ourselves back in that mindset since for the past 40 years we've lived in America where the overriding ideology has been we've got to not spend money on services.
sentences.zh: 要把我们自己带回那种心态非常困难，因为在过去的40年里，我们生活在美国，其压倒性的意识形态一直是：我们不能在公共服务上花钱。

sentences.en: This is the thing that we cannot spend much money on, whereas in the 1960s it was the exact opposite.
sentences.zh: 这是我们不能花太多钱的地方，而在20世纪60年代，情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: And the crisis in New York was one of those big tipping points in turning one from the other.
sentences.zh: 纽约的危机是导致这种转变的重大转折点之一。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, there was a sense up until this point, or maybe just especially during this time,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，直到这一点，或者也许特别是在这段时期，人们有一种感觉，

sentences.en: that there was a social contract with the big manufacturers and bankers and rich people that to make a society we all pitched in to create a better world for everybody.
sentences.zh: 即与大制造商、银行家和富人之间存在一种社会契约，为了建设一个社会，我们大家都出一份力，为每个人创造一个更美好的世界。

sentences.en: I think I would call it the we all live in the same country compact, which no longer exists.
sentences.zh: 我想我会称之为“我们生活在同一个国家”的契约，而这种契约已经不复存在了。

sentences.en: But at a certain point, and it sort of starts a little bit in the 60s and the 70s, there's off-ramps afforded the rich and the powerful to not put in their part.
sentences.zh: 但在某个时刻，这在60年代和70年代开始显现，富人和权贵们有了逃避责任的出口，不再履行他们的那部分义务。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, the economic underpinnings of the great society, like the wheels come off because rich people just kind of go, no, I'm not paying for that.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，“伟大社会”的经济基础就像轮子脱落了一样，因为富人们只是说，不，我才不为那个买单。

sentences.en: I'm going to move out of the city or I'm going to move my factory to Delaware or Texas or something.
sentences.zh: 我要搬出这个城市，或者我要把工厂搬到特拉华州或德克萨斯州之类的地方。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, when you don't have that anymore,
sentences.zh: 突然之间，当你不再拥有这些时，

sentences.en: this system that's all built on a virtuous cycle of money coming through and the rich people not extracting as much as they can.
sentences.zh: 这个建立在资金流入的良性循环之上，且富人没有尽可能榨取利益的体系，就崩溃了。

sentences.en: And now they extract almost exclusively.
sentences.zh: 而现在，他们几乎只剩下榨取了。

sentences.en: This is the very beginning of that.
sentences.zh: 这正是这一切的开端。

sentences.en: And so this whole system is like, it's not just that there's overspending liberals.
sentences.zh: 所以整个体系，不仅仅是因为有挥霍无度的自由派。

sentences.en: It's like we had a social contract with everybody that we were all making the world a better place.
sentences.zh: 而是我们曾经与每个人达成过社会契约，我们都在让世界变得更美好。

sentences.en: And the taxes reflected that.
sentences.zh: 税收也反映了这一点。

sentences.en: And people not moving their factories out away from where people lived reflected that.
sentences.zh: 人们没有把工厂搬离人们居住的地方，也反映了这一点。

sentences.en: It was all built on this system and it all comes apart.
sentences.zh: 这一切都建立在这个体系之上，而现在它分崩离析了。

sentences.en: And this is a big tension of this movie, Drop Dead City,
sentences.zh: 这也是这部电影《死城》的一大张力所在，

sentences.en: is like one of the breaking points in the sort of the fiscal crisis of New York is this idea of selling the municipal bonds that the banks would then bid on and then sell to their customers.
sentences.zh: 纽约财政危机的一个爆发点，就是这种出售市政债券的想法，银行会竞标，然后卖给他们的客户。

sentences.en: And there's this sense of the overspending, the bankruptcy is on the horizon.
sentences.zh: 人们感觉到挥霍无度，破产就在眼前。

sentences.en: And the banks decide, we're not going to buy your bonds.
sentences.zh: 银行决定：我们不买你们的债券了。

sentences.en: And it used to be competitive and they bid on it and then they would parcel them out.
sentences.zh: 过去这曾是竞争性的，他们会竞标，然后分销出去。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden,
sentences.zh: 突然之间，

sentences.en: this gear in the system of how the city pays for itself and pays for the services just starts to break down because the banks decide they do not want to take the risk of supporting these bonds because they do not know if the tax money is going to come in.
sentences.zh: 这个城市如何支付自身开支和公共服务的体系齿轮开始失灵，因为银行决定他们不想承担支持这些债券的风险，因为他们不知道税款是否会到位。

sentences.en: They are right to be skeptical of it because the tax money is not coming in.
sentences.zh: 他们怀疑是对的，因为税款确实没有到位。

sentences.en: It's not that they're wrong.
sentences.zh: 并不是他们错了。

sentences.en: It's just that up until this point, there was a shared fiction among everyone.
sentences.zh: 只是直到这一点，大家之间一直存在一种共同的虚构。

sentences.en: Everyone, it must have been just completely weird for Abe Beam, who is the mayor, who was the comptroller and becomes the mayor.
sentences.zh: 每个人，对于亚伯·比姆来说，这一定非常奇怪，他是市长，曾任审计长，后来当了市长。

sentences.en: And the new comptroller is named Harrison Gold and he does this independent audit and he's just like, the books don't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 新任审计长名叫哈里森·戈尔德，他进行了独立审计，他的结论是：账目根本不存在。

sentences.en: Nobody knows what anyone's making.
sentences.zh: 没人知道谁赚了多少钱。

sentences.en: The banks begin to like ask questions that are harder questions about whether or not the income coming in from these bonds is actually going to be paid.
sentences.zh: 银行开始提出更尖锐的问题，质疑这些债券带来的收入是否真的能兑现。

sentences.en: And in a way, you know, Beam felt attacked.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，你知道，比姆感到被冒犯了。

sentences.en: It's the kind of thing where if this was Enron, Golden would be a hero.
sentences.zh: 如果这是安然公司，戈尔德会是英雄。

sentences.en: He'd be a whistleblower.
sentences.zh: 他会是举报人。

sentences.en: But it's not Enron.
sentences.zh: 但这不是安然。

sentences.en: It's New York City.
sentences.zh: 这是纽约市。

sentences.en: And it's a lot of people live there.
sentences.zh: 那里住着很多人。

sentences.en: So there's much more at stake that's fraught.
sentences.zh: 所以赌注更大，情况更令人焦虑。

sentences.en: And Beam, there's so much of the story that is a story of changing generations in a way.
sentences.zh: 而比姆，这个故事中有很大一部分在某种程度上是关于代际更替的。

sentences.en: Beam is a fascinating character to me, partly because he is a very unfascinating person in a lot of ways.
sentences.zh: 比姆对我来说是一个迷人的人物，部分原因在于他在很多方面是一个非常平庸的人。

sentences.en: He's a short king.
sentences.zh: 他是个“矮个子国王”。

sentences.en: He's this short little guy.
sentences.zh: 他是个矮小的家伙。

sentences.en: He's an old school politician.
sentences.zh: 他是老派政客。

sentences.en: He came up through the machine.
sentences.zh: 他是通过政治机器爬上来的。

sentences.en: He came up in the days when you were a ward leader and you made sure that the people in your area had food on Christmas.
sentences.zh: 他成长于那个你是选区领导，确保你所在地区的人在圣诞节有饭吃的年代。

sentences.en: This guy needs a job.
sentences.zh: 这个人需要一份工作。

sentences.en: OK, I'll pull some strings to get you a job.
sentences.zh: 好，我找点关系帮你弄份工作。

sentences.en: And now he has become mayor in a new world where that kind of extremely hyper-local politics has been minimized or maybe vaporized by the interconnectedness of everything,
sentences.zh: 而现在他成了市长，在一个新的世界里，那种极度本土化的政治已经被最小化，或者因为万物互联而被蒸发了，

sentences.en: you know, and by new ways of doing things and more professional ways of doing things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，还有新的做事方式和更专业化的做事方式。

sentences.en: And banks that expect a more professional, more corporate level of governance than what he's used to, what he came up through.
sentences.zh: 银行期望的是比他习惯的、他所成长的环境更专业、更企业化的治理水平。

sentences.en: And I couldn't help compare him in my mind with the mayors that came after him, specifically when I was living in New York.
sentences.zh: 我忍不住在脑海中将他与他之后的市长们进行比较，特别是我住在纽约的时候。

sentences.en: And he's very much the opposite of Mayor Michael Bloomberg, who was mayor for three terms and was very much the – I'm a billionaire.
sentences.zh: 他与迈克尔·布隆伯格市长截然不同，后者连任三届，非常典型的——我是亿万富翁。

sentences.en: I ran a corporation.
sentences.zh: 我经营过一家公司。

sentences.en: I'm now going to run New York the way that a billionaire who runs a corporation would like New York to be run.
sentences.zh: 我现在要像一个经营公司的亿万富翁希望纽约被管理的那样去管理纽约。

sentences.en: Whereas Abe Beam was very much a guy who came up from the bottom and said, I'm going to try to run this city the way that a guy from the bottom might want it to be run,
sentences.zh: 而亚伯·比姆是一个从底层爬上来的人，他说，我要尝试用一个底层出身的人希望的方式来管理这座城市，

sentences.en: which is one where we try to give everybody the things that they need or want, and we don't worry as much about paying off bankers.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们尽量给每个人他们需要或想要的东西，而不必太担心偿还银行家。

sentences.en: And it just wasn't the right time in history for him to be doing that.
sentences.zh: 只是他在历史上的那个时刻做这件事，时机不对。

sentences.en: So the city is dependent on the bankers, thinking that the city is financially sound enough to do business with again.
sentences.zh: 所以城市依赖于银行家，认为城市在财务上足够稳健，可以再次与之做生意。

sentences.en: And the bankers wanted all sorts of city services cut for them to feel okay about investing in the city.
sentences.zh: 而银行家们想要削减各种城市服务，才能对投资这座城市感到安心。

sentences.en: And one of the main friction points between the banks and the city in terms of services was the City University of New York or CUNY.
sentences.zh: 银行与城市在服务方面的主要摩擦点之一是纽约市立大学，即CUNY。

sentences.en: CUNY is the city's public university system, and it had been tuition-free since its founding in 1847.
sentences.zh: CUNY是该市的公立大学系统，自1847年成立以来一直免收学费。

sentences.en: And Abe Beam is a graduate of CUNY, and he says all the time, I wouldn't be here.
sentences.zh: 亚伯·比姆是CUNY的毕业生，他总是说，我不会站在这里。

sentences.en: I wouldn't be mayor if it wasn't for free tuition.
sentences.zh: 如果不是因为免学费，我不会成为市长。

sentences.en: And it becomes such a symbol of to the bankers of what New York is doing wrong.
sentences.zh: 这成了银行家眼中纽约做错事的象征。

sentences.en: They think they can give free college to everybody in the city?
sentences.zh: 他们认为他们可以给城里的每个人提供免费大学教育？

sentences.en: This is insane.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Charge them tuition.
sentences.zh: 向他们收取学费。

sentences.en: And what the – I was going to say normal citizens.
sentences.zh: 而——我本来想说普通市民。

sentences.en: What the – let's say lower-wage citizens of New York believe,
sentences.zh: 而——让我们说纽约的低薪市民所相信的，

sentences.en: which is that the city is this shared place that owes services to them and which is there to help them to rise up in their status or their children to rise up in their station.
sentences.zh: 那就是这座城市是一个共享的地方，它欠他们服务，它是为了帮助他们提升地位，或者帮助他们的孩子提升地位而存在的。

sentences.en: And it is two competing views of what it means to live in a city and what it means to be American, and the city university just becomes this locus point of the fight.
sentences.zh: 这是关于生活在城市意味着什么以及成为美国人意味着什么的两种相互竞争的观点，而市立大学就成了这场斗争的焦点。

sentences.en: And it becomes something that the banks and the federal government become very offended by almost, like they're angry.
sentences.zh: 它变得让银行和联邦政府感到非常被冒犯，几乎就像他们很生气一样。

sentences.en: And they keep saying, don't you see?
sentences.zh: 他们一直说，难道你不明白吗？

sentences.en: You have to charge tuition because that will show the world that you're serious about being austere.
sentences.zh: 你必须收取学费，因为那会向世界表明你是认真对待紧缩政策的。

sentences.en: And it's such a – it becomes such a fracture point for just two different views of what it means to govern a city, you know, which are coming into crisis at this moment.
sentences.zh: 这成了一个断裂点，代表了关于治理城市意味着什么的两种不同观点，你知道，它们在这一刻陷入了危机。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And one of the things that's striking when you hear that as a main point of argument is how much the Overton window has shifted towards the banker's point of view.
sentences.zh: 当你听到这作为争论的重点时，令人震惊的一点是，奥弗顿之窗已经向银行家的观点倾斜了多少。

sentences.en: Now the argument is whether the government should help people to pay the hundreds of thousands of dollars that they owe in college rather than that the government should allow them to go to college for free.
sentences.zh: 现在的争论是政府是否应该帮助人们偿还他们欠下的数十万美元大学贷款，而不是政府是否应该让他们免费上大学。

sentences.en: It's really – it's an astonishing thing watching it and reading a little bit of supplementary materials afterwards.
sentences.zh: 这真的是——看着它，并在事后阅读一些补充材料，这是一件令人震惊的事情。

sentences.en: It was just such an astonishing vision of a different time when various services were just taken for granted as things that the New York City will provide.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个不同时代的惊人愿景，当时各种服务被视为理所当然，是纽约市会提供的。

sentences.en: And it wasn't like everybody in America was getting this, but that New York City took it for granted.
sentences.zh: 并不是说美国每个人都能得到这个，但纽约市把它视为理所当然。

sentences.en: This is part of living in the city as you get these things.
sentences.zh: 这是生活在城市的一部分，你会得到这些东西。

sentences.en: And it makes you wonder – the tradeoff is that then the city is running out of money and there's garbage all over the streets.
sentences.zh: 这让你怀疑——代价是城市资金枯竭，街道上到处都是垃圾。

sentences.en: But it's a tradeoff that often runs through my mind as someone who lived in New York during that different time post-Giuliani when Bloomberg was mayor.
sentences.zh: 但作为一个在那个不同时代，即朱利安尼之后、布隆伯格担任市长期间住在纽约的人，这个权衡经常在我脑海中浮现。

sentences.en: When the city contract seemed to be you are going to come here.
sentences.zh: 当时城市的契约似乎是：你会来到这里。

sentences.en: You're going to spend way more money than you think you should for your apartment.
sentences.zh: 你会为你的公寓支付比你认为应该支付的更多的钱。

sentences.en: You're going to work as hard as possible.
sentences.zh: 你会尽可能努力地工作。

sentences.en: The city is going to chew you up and spit you out.
sentences.zh: 这座城市会把你嚼碎并吐出来。

sentences.en: But the city is also safe and it's relatively clean.
sentences.zh: 但这座城市也是安全的，而且相对干净。

sentences.en: It still stinks.
sentences.zh: 它依然很臭。

sentences.en: Like the city still smells really bad, which my children always comment on every time we visit.
sentences.zh: 就像这座城市闻起来依然很糟糕，我孩子们每次来访时都会评论这一点。

sentences.en: But the idea that you can take it for granted that you're probably not going to get mugged.
sentences.zh: 但那种你可以认为你大概不会被抢劫是理所当然的想法。

sentences.en: Your building is probably not going to burn down.
sentences.zh: 你的大楼大概不会被烧毁。

sentences.en: Whereas in the 70s, it was almost like the opposite.
sentences.zh: 而在70年代，情况几乎恰恰相反。

sentences.en: It was almost like New York was entering this place where it was like you can go to college.
sentences.zh: 几乎就像纽约进入了一个地方，就像你可以上大学。

sentences.en: You'll have all these services.
sentences.zh: 你会拥有所有这些服务。

sentences.en: But it's also possible that you may get mugged.
sentences.zh: 但你也有可能被抢劫。

sentences.en: You may get stabbed.
sentences.zh: 你可能会被捅伤。

sentences.en: You might get caught in a fire.
sentences.zh: 你可能会卷入火灾。

sentences.en: The city is going to be filthy all over the place.
sentences.zh: 这座城市到处都会变得肮脏不堪。

sentences.en: I mean, it's still kind of filthy, but it just shows a – I guess the way to look at it is, I guess, as different priorities, you know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这依然有点混乱，但这恰恰表明——我想看待它的方式，大概就是把它看作不同的优先事项，你懂的。

sentences.en: And so this is a real inflection point in how the city is run financially, the sort of mindset of what services are, you know, just standard and which are far-reaching and,
sentences.zh: 所以，这在城市财政管理方式上是一个真正的转折点，关于什么是基本服务，什么是深远影响的服务，这种思维方式，你知道，

sentences.en: you know, like what we would consider to be kind of pipe dreams today in terms of what is being offered.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像我们今天认为的那些在所提供服务方面近乎白日梦的东西。

sentences.en: And what's funny is Nelson Rockefeller resigned and is no longer governor.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，纳尔逊·洛克菲勒辞职了，不再担任州长。

sentences.en: It feels like Beam is the last – the old guard kind of like holding on and everyone's like leaving him responsible to a certain extent.
sentences.zh: 感觉比姆（Beam）就像是最后一位——旧时代的卫道士，还在苦苦支撑，而每个人在某种程度上都把责任推给了他。

sentences.en: Rockefeller is like, I think I will be vice president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 洛克菲勒就像是说，我想我会去当美国副总统。

sentences.en: I'll let you deal with this.
sentences.zh: 这些事就留给你处理吧。

sentences.en: And so Hugh Carey is the new governor.
sentences.zh: 于是休·凯里（Hugh Carey）成了新任州长。

sentences.en: And he's also just like – he's been part of this the whole time.
sentences.zh: 他也只是——他一直以来都是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: And it probably, again, was kind of blindsided by like, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 而且他可能再次感到措手不及，心想，你这是什么意思？

sentences.en: We used to just do this this way and why is it a problem now?
sentences.zh: 我们过去一直都是这么做的，为什么现在就成了问题？

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: And really does not want to be the last one, you know, without a chair in musical chairs.
sentences.zh: 他真的不想成为玩抢椅子游戏时最后一个没椅子坐的人。

sentences.en: But it all comes down like the independent audit by Golden, this realization that, oh, you know, there's this sense of like maybe we're like $1 or $2 billion in debt.
sentences.zh: 但这一切都归结于戈尔登（Golden）的独立审计，人们意识到，哦，你知道，有一种感觉，也许我们欠债一二十亿美元。

sentences.en: And it turns out they're more like $6 billion in debt.
sentences.zh: 结果发现他们欠债高达60亿美元左右。

sentences.en: It feels like every time they do an audit, they find out that they are $2 billion more in debt than they were before.
sentences.zh: 感觉他们每次进行审计，都会发现比之前多出20亿美元的债务。

sentences.en: Like I don't know how expensive these audits were.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这些审计到底有多贵。

sentences.en: But, yeah, they keep thinking like it will be a little bit of a shortfall, but we'll be able to patch it up.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，他们一直以为这只是个小缺口，我们能补上。

sentences.en: And then they keep realizing how much bigger and bigger the bill is than they think it is, how much the city has been borrowing to cover its debt and how much it spends on things,
sentences.zh: 然后他们不断意识到账单比他们想象的要大得多，城市为了偿还债务借了多少钱，在各种事情上花了多少钱，

sentences.en: how much it's not taking in in terms of taxes.
sentences.zh: 在税收方面又少了多少收入。

sentences.en: Because it's really – I have to admit, I started getting very stressed just hearing about it in the movie.
sentences.zh: 因为这真的——我必须承认，光是在电影里听到这些，我就开始感到非常焦虑了。

sentences.en: And this happened 50 years ago and I wasn't involved.
sentences.zh: 而这发生在50年前，我当时还没参与其中。

sentences.en: So I was just like, oh, how are they going to get out of this one?
sentences.zh: 所以我当时就在想，哦，他们要怎么摆脱这个困境呢？

sentences.en: They never will, you know?
sentences.zh: 他们永远也摆脱不了，你懂吗？

sentences.en: And the sort of the shaky confidence is sort of like – the idea of people are not very confident about the city and its debt and its finances is getting to the bankers.
sentences.zh: 那种动摇的信心，就像是——人们对这座城市及其债务和财政状况缺乏信心，这让银行家们感到不安。

sentences.en: They're not buying the bonds anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们不再购买债券了。

sentences.en: That money coming in from buying the bonds was what was paying off the old bonds, which had been, you know, like set up decades before.
sentences.zh: 购买债券带来的资金正是用来偿还旧债券的，而那些旧债券，你知道，是几十年前就设立的。

sentences.en: And there's these series of crises in sort of 1975, which is like, oh, we're going to have a bunch of bonds due or we have to pay them off to the people who own them.
sentences.zh: 1975年左右发生了一系列危机，就像是，哦，我们要有一大批债券到期了，或者我们必须把钱还给债券持有人。

sentences.en: And if we don't have the money, we're going to default.
sentences.zh: 如果我们没有钱，我们就会违约。

sentences.en: And at first it's sort of like $10 million is due in like seven days and we have to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 起初就像是七天内有1000万美元到期，我们必须对此采取行动。

sentences.en: The bills always seem to be coming up in just a few days as if like no one was keeping a calendar of this at any point.
sentences.zh: 账单似乎总是在几天内就到期了，就好像从来没有人记过日程表一样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's always a bunch of bills that are coming up almost instantly and they continually have to find ways to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 总有一堆账单几乎立刻就要到期，他们必须不断寻找应对方法。

sentences.en: And they're only ways to raise more money or to make cuts.
sentences.zh: 而他们唯一的方法就是筹集更多资金或进行削减。

sentences.en: And so there's a quick reaction to all this like at first, which is like there's these construction projects and Beam just stops construction projects.
sentences.zh: 所以起初对这一切的反应很快，比如那些建设项目，比姆直接叫停了这些项目。

sentences.en: OK, so this is begin – like it's like if we can't afford stuff, we can't do it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是开始——就像如果我们负担不起，我们就不能做。

sentences.en: We can't pay the construction workers.
sentences.zh: 我们付不起建筑工人的工资。

sentences.en: And so the first – the construction workers, which are a nicely paid contingent of the electorate, all of a sudden don't have projects to work on.
sentences.zh: 所以首先——建筑工人，这群选民中薪水不错的一部分，突然之间没有项目可做了。

sentences.en: And so they get angry first, you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 所以他们首先感到愤怒，你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: And the things that are deteriorating begin deteriorating even more.
sentences.zh: 而那些正在恶化的事物开始变得更加糟糕。

sentences.en: And then there's a round of like laying off workers and there's even like a layoff of cops, which is – has never happened before in the city of New York.
sentences.zh: 然后是一轮裁员，甚至还裁减了警察，这在纽约市是前所未有的。

sentences.en: Apparently there have only been more and more cops over time up until that point.
sentences.zh: 显然，在那之前，警察人数一直都在增加。

sentences.en: There's a real growth industry was policing in New York and the cops go – they have this big protest action where they're shutting down a bridge.
sentences.zh: 纽约的警务工作曾是一个真正的增长行业，警察们开始行动——他们举行了一场大规模抗议活动，封锁了一座桥梁。

sentences.en: Like you have police officers off-duty protesting who are getting into fights with police officers that are there to try to keep the peace on duty.
sentences.zh: 就像你看到下班的警察在抗议，并与那些在现场维持秩序的执勤警察发生冲突。

sentences.en: And I mean the term powder keg gets thrown around a lot.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是“火药桶”这个词被频繁提及。

sentences.en: But I think that was the fear at the time was if New York defaults, you're going to get even more of this,
sentences.zh: 但我认为当时人们担心的是，如果纽约违约，这种情况会愈演愈烈，

sentences.en: that it's such a powder keg that we're going to have to fire cops and they're going to be rioting.
sentences.zh: 因为它就像一个火药桶，我们不得不解雇警察，然后他们会引发骚乱。

sentences.en: We're going to have to fire sanitation workers and the garbage is going to pile up.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不解雇环卫工人，垃圾会堆积如山。

sentences.en: We're going to have to fire firefighters at a time when there's fires constantly in the city because there are abandoned buildings going up in flames.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不解雇消防员，而当时城市里火灾不断，因为废弃的建筑物都在起火。

sentences.en: There are landlords who are getting buildings off of their hands by lighting them on fire.
sentences.zh: 有些房东通过纵火来摆脱手中的建筑。

sentences.en: And all these very basic services and the people who are being cut are not like, oh, well, I guess it's time for me to go pick up the skills for another job.
sentences.zh: 所有这些非常基础的服务，而那些被裁掉的人并不是说，哦，好吧，我想我该去学点其他工作的技能了。

sentences.en: No, they could react very angrily and there's a feeling of, but we're supposed to have the power in this relationship because we're these powerful unions.
sentences.zh: 不，他们的反应非常愤怒，有一种感觉是，我们本应在这段关系中拥有权力，因为我们是这些强大的工会。

sentences.en: And it becomes to a certain extent – if I can use the term pissing match on this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上变成了——如果我可以在这个播客里用这个词的话——一场撒尿比赛。

sentences.en: It becomes a little bit of one of those, but just these things that the city has not seen in a long, long time.
sentences.zh: 它变得有点像那样，但这些都是这座城市很久很久没有见过的事情。

sentences.en: And the fear is if we cut all these services, then the city is going to be – it's going to turn into bedlam.
sentences.zh: 人们担心的是，如果我们削减所有这些服务，那么这座城市将会——它会变成一片混乱。

sentences.en: People are just going to riot and rise up.
sentences.zh: 人们只会暴动和反抗。

sentences.en: But also if we don't make these cuts, the city is going to default,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们不进行这些削减，城市就会违约，

sentences.en: in which case everyone is going to lose their job and the city is going to rise up and it will be riots and become violent if these things happen.
sentences.zh: 那样的话，每个人都会失业，城市会反抗，如果这些事情发生，就会演变成骚乱和暴力。

sentences.en: The police union really pushes this narrative and they even launch a propaganda campaign where off-duty cops go to bus terminals and they pass out pamphlets to tourists that say like in big letters,
sentences.zh: 警察工会真的在推行这种叙事，他们甚至发起了一场宣传运动，下班的警察去巴士总站向游客散发传单，上面用大字写着，

sentences.en: welcome to fear city with a grim reaper in the middle.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到恐惧之城，中间画着一个死神。

sentences.en: And underneath it, it said a survival guide for visitors to the city of New York.
sentences.zh: 下面写着：纽约市游客生存指南。

sentences.en: All these tips where it's like don't leave your hotel room after dark.
sentences.zh: 上面有各种提示，比如天黑后不要离开酒店房间。

sentences.en: Do not ride the subways.
sentences.zh: 不要乘坐地铁。

sentences.en: Like they're really raising the level of paranoia among travelers especially because what they're trying to do is they're trying to say if we're not on duty,
sentences.zh: 他们真的在提高游客的偏执程度，尤其是因为他们试图说的是，如果我们不在岗，

sentences.en: we are going to cut off the tourism to New York City that amazingly, even at this time when New York City was crumbling, was still pretty big business.
sentences.zh: 我们将切断纽约市的旅游业，令人惊讶的是，即使在纽约市摇摇欲坠的时候，这仍然是一门相当大的生意。

sentences.en: That's the thing that's astounding to me is that – and New York is an enormous city.
sentences.zh: 这才是让我感到震惊的地方——而且纽约是一个巨大的城市。

sentences.en: What's happening in one side of the city is so different from what's happening on the other side of the city.
sentences.zh: 城市一侧发生的事情与另一侧发生的事情截然不同。

sentences.en: What's happening in the South Bronx is so different from what's happening in Greenwich Village, which is so different from what's happening in Flushing, Queens.
sentences.zh: 南布朗克斯发生的事情与格林威治村发生的事情截然不同，而这又与法拉盛发生的事情截然不同。

sentences.en: Like it's an enormous city.
sentences.zh: 它真是一个巨大的城市。

sentences.en: But you see this footage of garbage in the streets, old buildings just crumbling, just empty lots of rubble that children are playing in and getting hurt in.
sentences.zh: 但你看到街头垃圾的画面，旧建筑在倒塌，孩子们在满是瓦砾的空地上玩耍并受伤。

sentences.en: And at the same time, it's still – people still want to go to New York and visit it.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，它依然——人们仍然想去纽约参观。

sentences.en: Like they still want to see the Empire State Building and Times Square and even though Times Square is full of at that point just kind of like porn theaters and shooting galleries and things like that.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然想看帝国大厦和时代广场，尽管当时的时代广场到处都是色情影院、射击场之类的东西。

sentences.en: Like they still want to go see these things.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然想去看看这些东西。

sentences.en: And the police are – they want to present the idea that without – if you don't rehire these police, without this police presence, the city will just be the most dangerous,
sentences.zh: 而警察们——他们想传达这样一个观点：如果不重新雇佣这些警察，没有这种警力存在，这座城市将成为世界上最危险、

sentences.en: frightening place in the world.
sentences.zh: 最可怕的地方。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the city is trying to figure out where it's going to get all this money.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，市政府正试图弄清楚从哪里筹集所有这些资金。

sentences.en: So they approach the federal government.
sentences.zh: 于是他们求助于联邦政府。

sentences.en: So Nixon had resigned a year earlier and Gerald Ford is now the president.
sentences.zh: 尼克松在一年前辞职了，杰拉尔德·福特现在是总统。

sentences.en: And like we mentioned, former New York governor, Nelson Rockefeller,
sentences.zh: 正如我们提到的，前纽约州州长纳尔逊·洛克菲勒，

sentences.en: had gotten himself appointed as vice president and the secretary of treasury was William Simon who had been a New York City bond salesman.
sentences.zh: 已经让自己被任命为副总统，而财政部长是威廉·西蒙（William Simon），他曾是一名纽约市债券推销员。

sentences.en: So like they knew exactly what had been going on in the city.
sentences.zh: 所以他们非常清楚城市里发生了什么。

sentences.en: You would think – you would think the vice president used to be our governor.
sentences.zh: 你会认为——你会认为副总统曾经是我们的州长。

sentences.en: The secretary of treasury used to live – work here.
sentences.zh: 财政部长曾经住在这里——在这里工作。

sentences.en: This will be super easy.
sentences.zh: 这应该超级简单。

sentences.en: But it's the – instead, it's the exact opposite.
sentences.zh: 但事实恰恰相反。

sentences.en: It's such a stonewall.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一堵墙。

sentences.en: And Simon is part of the problem.
sentences.zh: 西蒙也是问题的一部分。

sentences.en: But another part of the problem is who is running things in the Ford administration and like my stomach hurt when these guys showed up in the movie.
sentences.zh: 但问题的另一部分是福特政府的掌权者是谁，当这些家伙出现在电影里时，我的胃都疼了。

sentences.en: It's Donald Rumsfeld and Dick Cheney.
sentences.zh: 是唐纳德·拉姆斯菲尔德和迪克·切尼。

sentences.en: What is going – like how many times are they going to pop up in the government and wreck things and just do bad stuff?
sentences.zh: 到底是怎么回事——他们还要在政府里出现多少次，搞砸事情，做坏事？

sentences.en: Like it's – they're just such bad guys.
sentences.zh: 他们简直就是坏人。

sentences.en: You know, it was like – I don't know if you had the same reaction I did, Roman,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就像——我不知道你是否有和我一样的反应，罗曼，

sentences.en: but it was literally like as soon as they showed up on screen looking young and smiling because they're doing bad – they're hurting people and they love it.
sentences.zh: 但当他们出现在屏幕上，看起来年轻且面带微笑时，那感觉简直就像——因为他们在做坏事——他们在伤害别人，而且他们乐在其中。

sentences.en: I was like, oh, these guys.
sentences.zh: 我就想，哦，又是这些家伙。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: How do they keep doing it?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么能一直这样？

sentences.en: These bad pennies keep turning up.
sentences.zh: 这些坏家伙总是阴魂不散。

sentences.en: It's totally right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: It's like watching the Star Wars prequels and you see like, you know, like Senator Palpatine walking across and you're like, I know what you're – I know what's going to happen now.
sentences.zh: 这就像看《星球大战》前传，你看到帕尔帕廷议员走过来，你会想，我知道你要做什么——我知道接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: More on Drop Dead City after the break.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，继续讨论《死城》（Drop Dead City）。

sentences.en: We're back with Elliot Kalin talking about the documentary Drop Dead City.
sentences.zh: 我们回来了，继续与埃利奥特·卡林（Elliot Kalin）讨论纪录片《死城》。

sentences.en: So when we left New York, it was 1975 and the city was trying to claw its way out of a catastrophic financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们离开纽约时，那是1975年，这座城市正试图从一场灾难性的金融危机中挣扎出来。

sentences.en: The federal government did not want to help and so the city is stuck sort of negotiating between the bankers who want deep cuts to services and the city workers who want their jobs.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府不想提供帮助，所以这座城市陷入了困境，在想要大幅削减服务的银行家和想要保住工作的城市工人之间进行谈判。

sentences.en: And so you end up in this cycle of the city constantly firing people, cutting services, strikes happening because the unions are mad because of the services,
sentences.zh: 于是你陷入了一个循环：城市不断裁员、削减服务，工会因为服务问题而愤怒并举行罢工，

sentences.en: talks between the bankers and the city, talks between the unions and the city and the formation of different schemes to try to reorganize the city's finances.
sentences.zh: 银行家与城市之间的谈判，工会与城市之间的谈判，以及为重组城市财政而制定的各种计划。

sentences.en: And the big one is MAC, the Municipal Assistance Corporation, under the oversight of Chairman Felix Rohatyn.
sentences.zh: 其中最主要的是MAC，即市政援助公司，在主席菲利克斯·罗哈廷（Felix Rohatyn）的监督下。

sentences.en: I always cannot quite – his name is spelled R-O-H-A-T-Y-N and I always have trouble pronouncing it in my head.
sentences.zh: 我总是无法完全——他的名字拼写是R-O-H-A-T-Y-N，我在心里总是很难读准它。

sentences.en: You know, in the movie they say it a couple of different ways, but I sort of make it rhyme with Manhattan, Felix Rohatyn.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在电影里他们有几种不同的读法，但我倾向于让它和曼哈顿（Manhattan）押韵，菲利克斯·罗哈廷。

sentences.en: Oh, that's really nice.
sentences.zh: 哦，那真的很好。

sentences.en: That's a good way to do it.
sentences.zh: 那是个好办法。

sentences.en: And at this point, if you wanted to put it into political cartoon terms, it becomes in some ways the bankers versus the unions where the bankers are saying you need to make cuts.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，如果你想用政治漫画的术语来说，它在某些方面变成了银行家对阵工会，银行家说你需要削减开支。

sentences.en: You need to make cuts.
sentences.zh: 你需要削减开支。

sentences.en: And the unions are saying, no, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 而工会说，不，不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: Don't make cuts.
sentences.zh: 不要削减开支。

sentences.en: We're going to go on strike if you do this.
sentences.zh: 如果你这样做，我们就罢工。

sentences.en: And the city is kind of paralyzed in the middle.
sentences.zh: 而城市在中间处于瘫痪状态。

sentences.en: But it's really more complicated than that because so much of the solution to the problem involves also the unions investing in these bonds as well,
sentences.zh: 但这比那复杂得多，因为解决问题的很大一部分还涉及工会也投资这些债券，

sentences.en: which is something that I was not as familiar with and seems very strange to me because it's like, well,
sentences.zh: 这对我来说不太熟悉，而且看起来非常奇怪，因为，好吧，

sentences.en: now the union pension fund is going to invest in the city that then pays the union workers.
sentences.zh: 现在工会养老基金要投资于这座城市，然后城市再支付给工会工人。

sentences.en: And if it works, what a beautiful cycle of money that can just go in and out of the union pockets and out of the city pockets.
sentences.zh: 如果这行得通，那真是一个美丽的资金循环，可以进出工会的口袋，也可以进出城市的口袋。

sentences.en: But it really shows you I guess that the narrative that I was always taught growing up was the city ran out of money because it was too poorly managed and it didn't know what it was doing and it needed help and it had to cut everything in order to get bankers to come back and businesses to come back.
sentences.zh: 但这确实向你展示了，我想，我从小被灌输的叙事是：城市因为管理不善、不知道自己在做什么而耗尽了资金，它需要帮助，必须削减一切才能让银行家和企业回来。

sentences.en: And it had to become the technotopian of capitalist world that is right now.
sentences.zh: 它必须成为现在这种资本主义世界的科技乌托邦。

sentences.en: But in reality, it's a much more complicated story and one that didn't come to as clean a conclusion as it's sometimes told,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这是一个复杂得多的故事，而且并没有像有时讲述的那样有一个干净利落的结局，

sentences.en: but also still relied on a lot of different power brokers and power sources having to come together to work together in some way.
sentences.zh: 它仍然依赖于许多不同的权力掮客和权力来源，他们必须以某种方式走到一起共同努力。

sentences.en: This whole idea of this municipal assistance corporation is basically there to find wonky ways to create new kinds of bonds so that maybe if the MAC is sponsoring the bonds of the city,
sentences.zh: 这个市政援助公司的整个想法基本上是为了找到巧妙的方法来创造新型债券，这样如果MAC为城市债券提供担保，

sentences.en: you know, like it has a little bit more confidence in terms of the bankers.
sentences.zh: 你知道，银行家们对它就会多一点信心。

sentences.en: This will show the banks that somebody is overseeing the city in a way that's going to keep it honeSt.
sentences.zh: 这将向银行表明，有人在监督这座城市，以确保它保持诚实。

sentences.en: And I love also that they need a that they need a great acronym for it and they start calling it Big Mac, which is such a it's just that branding is so important,
sentences.zh: 我也很喜欢他们需要一个很棒的缩写，他们开始称之为“巨无霸”（Big Mac），这真是——品牌推广太重要了，

sentences.en: even in something like this.
sentences.zh: 即使在这样的事情中也是如此。

sentences.en: And the way people perceive things is so important, even in something as seemingly boring and cut and dry as municipal bond confidence, you know.
sentences.zh: 人们感知事物的方式非常重要，即使是在市政债券信心这种看似枯燥和简单的事情上，你知道。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Big Mac comes in, it begins to diminish Mayor Bean, who's just sort of there for, you know, ceremonial things and is not making the fiscal decisions of the city,
sentences.zh: 所以“巨无霸”介入了，它开始削弱比姆市长，他只是在那里处理一些礼仪性的事务，并没有做出城市的财政决策，

sentences.en: which you could argue is like the key decisions of a mayor.
sentences.zh: 你可以说这才是市长的关键决策。

sentences.en: And I would say so.
sentences.zh: 我会这么说。

sentences.en: And then they can't get a break from, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后他们无法得到喘息的机会，你知道，

sentences.en: like he goes and testifies in front of subcommittees where these Alabama senators are like chastising them for their spending habits and stuff like this.
sentences.zh: 他去小组委员会作证，那些阿拉巴马州的参议员们像这样指责他们的消费习惯等等。

sentences.en: It's like the whole place is really, really shaky.
sentences.zh: 就像整个地方真的非常非常不稳定。

sentences.en: Now, what we all have to consider is how the people back in our respective states respond to this.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们所有人都必须考虑我们各自州的人民对此有何反应。

sentences.en: If we're going to help you out, we've got to justify it to them.
sentences.zh: 如果我们打算帮助你们，我们必须向他们证明其合理性。

sentences.en: And right now we're having great difficulty doing it.
sentences.zh: 而现在我们在这方面遇到了很大的困难。

sentences.en: Now, you noted yourself that New York has the strongest municipal unions in the nation.
sentences.zh: 你刚才自己也提到，纽约拥有全国最强大的市政工会。

sentences.en: I suggest that they're too strong and the salaries are inordinately high in New York.
sentences.zh: 我建议他们太强大了，纽约的薪水高得离谱。

sentences.en: That feeling that New York needs to be disciplined, that it needs to be punished, that it is a place that can barely hold together.
sentences.zh: 那种认为纽约需要被管教、需要被惩罚、它是一个几乎无法维持下去的地方的感觉。

sentences.en: And it's full of just the most violent, uncontrollable, liberal scum of the country, which has its incredible layers of racism built into that.
sentences.zh: 而且它充满了全国最暴力、最不可控的自由派人渣，其中内置了令人难以置信的种族主义色彩。

sentences.en: You know, that so much of this is black migrants from the south coming up to New York.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这其中很大一部分是来自南方的黑人移民来到纽约。

sentences.en: This is Puerto Ricans coming to New York City, people who are not middle class white homeowners.
sentences.zh: 这是波多黎各人来到纽约市，那些不是中产阶级白人房主的人。

sentences.en: That is all built into this.
sentences.zh: 这一切都内置在其中。

sentences.en: But this idea that someone's got to teach New York a lesson.
sentences.zh: 但这种必须有人给纽约上一课的想法。

sentences.en: No, it's the it's the worSt.
sentences.zh: 不，这是最糟糕的。

sentences.en: And there and there's this rise of conservatism like Gerald Ford.
sentences.zh: 而且——而且出现了像杰拉尔德·福特那样的保守主义抬头。

sentences.en: I don't have much of an impression of him.
sentences.zh: 我对他的印象并不深。

sentences.en: He was, you know, you know, that whole administration was an unelected administration.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你知道，整个那届政府都是未经选举产生的政府。

sentences.en: You know, he was I'll give you the Reader's Digest version of Gerald Ford.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我给你讲讲杰拉尔德·福特的“读者文摘”版简史吧。

sentences.en: Gerald Ford, well-meaning guy, not particularly ideological, but very kind of like, well, everyone's got to follow a budget.
sentences.zh: 杰拉尔德·福特，是个好心人，没什么特别的意识形态，但给人的感觉就是，嗯，每个人都得遵守预算。

sentences.en: He loves budgets and he doesn't like the idea of spending very athletic, incredibly probably the most athletic president we've ever had.
sentences.zh: 他热爱预算，不喜欢花钱，而且他身体素质极好，大概是我们历任总统中身体素质最好的一位。

sentences.en: Could have played professional ball, football, that is.
sentences.zh: 他本可以打职业球赛，我是说橄榄球。

sentences.en: But, yeah, unelected to where he is.
sentences.zh: 但是，没错，他上任时确实未经选举。

sentences.en: And the feeling I always get from him is someone who is not really equipped to handle the job that he is doing.
sentences.zh: 我对他一直以来的感觉是，他并没有真正胜任他所做的工作。

sentences.en: Not he's not an idiot, but that he is struggling more because he does not have a real strong ideological bearing.
sentences.zh: 他不是个白痴，但他之所以挣扎，更多是因为他缺乏真正坚定的意识形态立场。

sentences.en: And so when this is all happening with New York City,
sentences.zh: 所以，当这一切发生在纽约市时，

sentences.en: what's really in the back of his mind other than New York needs to be taught a lesson because everyone needs to live within a budget is I know in 1976 I'm going to face Ronald Reagan in the presidential primary.
sentences.zh: 他脑子里真正想的，除了“纽约需要接受教训，因为每个人都必须在预算内生活”之外，就是我知道1976年我将在总统初选中面对罗纳德·里根。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Ronald Reagan is going to say we need to cut taxes and we need to cut services.
sentences.zh: 而罗纳德·里根会说我们需要减税，我们需要削减服务。

sentences.en: So I got to outflank him on the right and it just shows you how any decision made by someone in an elected federal office is partly about the decision and partly about how is this going to affect me in the next election.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须在右翼立场上胜过他，这恰恰说明了任何民选联邦官员所做的决定，部分是关于决定本身，部分是关于这会如何影响我的下一次选举。

sentences.en: And I think it can't be understated how much Gerald Ford was taking a cue from the people who worked for him who were much more conservative than he was and also attempting to set himself up not as I'm the Republican presidential candidate who saved New York by giving it an unlimited lifeline of money,
sentences.zh: 我认为怎么强调都不为过，杰拉尔德·福特在多大程度上听取了他手下那些比他保守得多的人的建议，同时也试图将自己定位——不是那种通过提供无限资金救助纽约来拯救城市的共和党总统候选人，

sentences.en: this city that all of us conservatives hate, but instead how he's trying to kind of out Reagan Reagan in that moment.
sentences.zh: 不是我们这些保守派所憎恨的城市，而是他试图在那个时刻以某种方式在里根之上超越里根。

sentences.en: And he doesn't do it in the most tactful way.
sentences.zh: 而且他做得并不圆滑。

sentences.en: In the documentary Ford's communications director, David Gergen says he got a call to write a speech for Ford explaining why he would not support any help to New York City.
sentences.zh: 在纪录片中，福特的通讯主管大卫·格根说，他接到电话要为福特写一篇演讲稿，解释为什么他不支持对纽约市的任何援助。

sentences.en: I had the impression that Ford wanted a hardline speech.
sentences.zh: 我当时的感觉是福特想要一篇强硬的演讲稿。

sentences.en: So I wrote a very hard-hitting speech and sent it over with the understanding it was going to be staffed out.
sentences.zh: 所以我写了一篇非常有力的演讲稿，并把它发了过去，以为会经过工作人员的润色。

sentences.en: And what happens in the staffing now is it gets watered down.
sentences.zh: 而润色的结果就是它被淡化了。

sentences.en: I was shocked when he gave a speech.
sentences.zh: 他发表那篇演讲时，我感到震惊。

sentences.en: The responsibility for New York City's financial problems is being left on the front doorstep of the federal government, unwanted and abandoned by its real parents.
sentences.zh: 纽约市财政问题的责任被留在了联邦政府的门阶上，被其真正的父母所遗弃和抛弃。

sentences.en: I can tell you and tell you now that I am prepared to veto any bill that has as its purpose a federal bailout of New York City to prevent a default.
sentences.zh: 我现在就可以告诉你，我准备否决任何旨在通过联邦救助纽约市以防止违约的法案。

sentences.en: I am fundamentally opposed to this so-called solution.
sentences.zh: 我从根本上反对这种所谓的解决方案。

sentences.en: Ford gives this speech on October 29th, 1975.
sentences.zh: 福特在1975年10月29日发表了这篇演讲。

sentences.en: And the next day, the New York Daily News runs a front-page story with the headline, Ford to City, Drop Dead.
sentences.zh: 第二天，《纽约每日新闻》在头版刊登了一篇报道，标题是“福特对城市说：去死吧”。

sentences.en: Of course, Ford never said those exact words, like really anything like those words, but it did not matter.
sentences.zh: 当然，福特从未说过那样的原话，甚至连类似的话都没说过，但这并不重要。

sentences.en: When it was run through the New York Daily News translation machine, we end up with the headline, Ford to City, Drop Dead.
sentences.zh: 当它通过《纽约每日新闻》的翻译机器处理后，我们最终得到了“福特对城市说：去死吧”这个标题。

sentences.en: Which is such – I mean when you think about the greatest headlines in American history in newspaper, it's like man walks on moon, Dewey defeats Truman,
sentences.zh: 这真是——我的意思是，当你想到美国历史上最伟大的报纸头条时，就像“人类登上月球”、“杜威击败杜鲁门”，

sentences.en: and Dewey defeats Truman just gets in because it's that great picture because they were wrong.
sentences.zh: 而“杜威击败杜鲁门”之所以能入选，是因为那张伟大的照片，因为他们当时搞错了。

sentences.en: And Ford to City, Drop Dead.
sentences.zh: 还有“福特对城市说：去死吧”。

sentences.en: And then I think it was the Post had headless body found in topless bar, which is one of the all-time great New York newspaper headlines.
sentences.zh: 然后我想《邮报》还有“无头尸体在无上装酒吧被发现”，这是纽约报纸史上最伟大的头条之一。

sentences.en: But the fact that this headline felt to New Yorkers like it so captured the feeling they were getting from the federal government and it so tainted the idea of Ford's response in the minds of New Yorkers in a way that you can argue whether it was fair or not.
sentences.zh: 但这个标题让纽约人觉得它如此精准地捕捉到了他们从联邦政府那里感受到的情绪，并且在纽约人的心目中玷污了福特的回应，至于这是否公平，你可以争论。

sentences.en: But I will say it's a great headline, so I'm OK with it.
sentences.zh: 但我得说这是一个伟大的头条，所以我没意见。

sentences.en: It's really a moment where you see the power of journalism because one of the things that's so fascinating about the Ford like tough speech and the New York Daily News' Ford to City,
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个让你看到新闻力量的时刻，因为关于福特那篇强硬的演讲和《纽约每日新闻》的“福特对城市说：去死吧”标题，最迷人的一点是，

sentences.zh: 这才是这一切的真正核心。

sentences.en: The services would not be necessary if the city was easier to live in, you know, and was also contributing to the city's just lack of spending cash on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 如果这座城市更容易居住，这些服务本来是不必要的，你知道，而且城市也不至于每天都面临资金短缺的问题。

sentences.en: You know, you can't run a city on the tolls on the tribal bridge, but you could probably like keep it afloat for a couple of days if you needed to.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你不能靠部落大桥的过路费来维持一座城市，但如果需要的话，你大概能让它维持运转几天。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想你是对的。

sentences.en: I think his sort of ability to sequester and isolate this little like business of the tribal authority and keep it away from the general operating expenses of New York.
sentences.zh: 我认为他那种将部落管理局的这点小生意隔离和孤立起来，并使其远离纽约一般运营开支的能力。

sentences.en: And there's there's really no reason why if you just weren't so obsessed with roads and to lesser extent parks that you wouldn't think that this money coming in could not support public transit or other services and just realize this is an income stream that is part of of New York and New York should use it as it best sees fit.
sentences.zh: 而且真的没有理由，如果你不是那么痴迷于道路，在较小程度上是公园，你不会认为这些进账的钱可以支持公共交通或其他服务，并意识到这是一种属于纽约的收入来源，纽约应该以它认为最合适的方式使用它。

sentences.en: Whereas Robert Moses wrote all the laws and controlled everything so that he got to see where that money went to and how to create these shovel ready projects to get from the feds.
sentences.zh: 而罗伯特·摩西编写了所有的法律并控制了一切，这样他就能看到钱流向哪里，以及如何创造这些现成的项目来从联邦政府那里获得资金。

sentences.en: And, you know, like you could say that, you know, maybe that wouldn't have worked as well had he, you know, like people being able to get to that money and use it for other things.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你可以说，如果人们能够接触到那笔钱并将其用于其他事情，也许这不会那么有效。

sentences.en: But yet that would be great if he didn't get his way.
sentences.zh: 但如果他没能如愿以偿，那会很棒。

sentences.en: And, you know, maybe a few different highways wouldn't have been built and some money wouldn't have flowed through the system.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，也许几条不同的高速公路就不会被修建，一些钱也不会流经这个系统。

sentences.en: But that again, like if fractions of that had been devoted to the subway system, we wouldn't have the breakdown of the subway system later on,
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，如果其中一小部分能投入到地铁系统中，我们后来就不会出现地铁系统崩溃的情况，

sentences.en: which is a huge part of this crisis in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 这在70年代的危机中占了很大一部分。

sentences.en: And so much of this that I think, you know, he's not responsible for six billion dollars of deficit,
sentences.zh: 我认为这其中很大一部分，你知道，他并不对六十亿美元的赤字负责，

sentences.en: but had he thought in the totality about the health and welfare of New York and New Yorkers and really had that at the center of his like his heart and soul.
sentences.zh: 但如果他从整体上考虑纽约和纽约人的健康与福利，并真正将其放在他内心深处。

sentences.en: This place really could have avoided this.
sentences.zh: 这个地方本可以避免这种情况。

sentences.en: I mean, like it would require a different structure of system, but I feel like he was smart enough that he could figure that out if he just cared about these things.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这需要一个不同的系统结构，但我觉得他足够聪明，如果他真的关心这些事情，他就能想出办法。

sentences.en: And so I would put a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以我投入了很多。

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard to, you know, run the tape back and see how history would have played out had he, you know, been a true New Yorker team player and cared about.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很难回溯过去，看看如果他是一个真正的纽约团队合作者并关心这一切，历史会如何发展。

sentences.en: As Robert Caro says, you can't say if New York would be a better city without Robert Moser.
sentences.zh: 正如罗伯特·卡罗所说，你不能说没有罗伯特·摩西，纽约会成为一个更好的城市。

sentences.en: It would be a different city.
sentences.zh: 它会是一个不同的城市。

sentences.en: But I do think that there's a good chance it could have been actually better if he had all those powers and all that faculty to build and create and make things and also thought about the city as a whole and cared about all the different aspects of who is in the city.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，如果他拥有所有这些权力和能力去建设、创造和制造事物，同时也把城市作为一个整体来考虑，并关心城市中所有不同方面的人，那么它很有可能实际上会变得更好。

sentences.en: I think that there was a tool at the disposal of the city to make this better and maybe not have this crisis happen at all.
sentences.zh: 我认为城市手中有一个工具可以让情况变得更好，也许根本就不会发生这场危机。

sentences.en: And Robert Moses could have been that tool, you know.
sentences.zh: 而罗伯特·摩西本可以成为那个工具，你知道。

sentences.en: You put your finger on something, Roman, too, that I had forgotten about because I'm so focused on the physical, the tangible, you know, roads, tunnels, bridges, parks,
sentences.zh: 罗曼，你也指出了我忽略的一点，因为我太专注于物质、有形的东西，你知道，道路、隧道、桥梁、公园，

sentences.en: that you're right that you mentioned he wrote the laws.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，你提到他编写了法律。

sentences.en: And one of New York's problems was that it could not raise certain taxes unless the state gave it approval.
sentences.zh: 纽约的问题之一是，除非得到州的批准，否则它无法提高某些税收。

sentences.en: Like there were institutional reasons that New York was kind of stuck in doing things the way it was.
sentences.zh: 就像纽约在做事方式上陷入困境是有制度原因的。

sentences.en: And he was responsible for at least some of those laws.
sentences.zh: 而他至少对其中一些法律负有责任。

sentences.en: He wrote the state constitution for New York, right?
sentences.zh: 他为纽约编写了州宪法，对吧？

sentences.en: So he is somewhat responsible for it directly even just from that.
sentences.zh: 所以即使仅从这一点来看，他也直接负有一定责任。

sentences.en: And I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 我想你是对的。

sentences.en: If he had been writing those laws less to an eye of how do I create little loopholes for myself in the future for doing powerful things and more from a point of view of that earlier Moses that we want to believe in from the beginning of the book who is more idealistic,
sentences.zh: 如果他在编写这些法律时，不是为了考虑如何为自己将来做有权势的事情创造小漏洞，而是从我们想要在书的开头相信的那个更理想主义的早期摩西的角度出发，

sentences.en: you know, even if we don't agree with all of his ideals.
sentences.zh: 你知道，即使我们不同意他的所有理想。

sentences.en: Then perhaps the city would have still found itself in a tight spot,
sentences.zh: 那么也许这座城市仍然会发现自己处于困境中，

sentences.en: but would have had the tools to wriggle out of that tight spot without things coming to a head so dramatically and so explosively.
sentences.zh: 但会有工具摆脱这种困境，而不会让事情如此戏剧性、如此爆发性地达到顶点。

sentences.en: On the other hand, think about it this way, Roman.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，换个角度想想，罗曼。

sentences.en: If there hadn't been that crisis, what would we be talking about on this episode today?
sentences.zh: 如果没有那场危机，我们今天在这一集里会谈论什么？

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: You're not going to do a whole episode on how New York sailed through the 70s fiscal bumpiness, you know?
sentences.zh: 你不会专门做一集关于纽约如何平稳度过70年代财政动荡的节目，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And 50 years later, we would have never met.
sentences.zh: 而且50年后，我们永远不会见面。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是真的。

sentences.en: So really, in a way, everything worked out for the beSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，从某种意义上说，一切都朝着最好的方向发展了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是真的。

sentences.en: Hey, it was fun revisiting The Power Broker and watching this movie, Drop Dead City.
sentences.zh: 嘿，重温《权力掮客》并观看这部电影《死城》很有趣。

sentences.en: If you haven't watched it already, I really recommend you check it out.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没看过，我真的建议你去看看。

sentences.en: If nothing else, just to hear the New Yorkers talk in the 1970s is the greatest thing in the world.
sentences.zh: 如果没什么别的，光是听听1970年代纽约人的谈话就是世界上最棒的事情。

sentences.en: And yeah, this is great.
sentences.zh: 是的，这太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Elliot, for rejoining us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，埃利奥特，再次加入我们。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.zh: 任何时候你想谈论纽约以及它能变得多么肮脏，请邀请我。

sentences.en: I would really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我将不胜感激。

sentences.zh: 《死城》将于11月14日在视频点播平台上发布。

sentences.zh: 如果你住在纽约，即将会有很多放映活动。

sentences.zh: 你可以在dropdeadcitythemovie.com了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And if you're interested in 1970s New York, but never got around to listening to our Power Broker breakdown series, then do yourself a favor.
sentences.zh: 如果你对1970年代的纽约感兴趣，但一直没时间听我们的《权力掮客》解析系列，那就帮自己一个忙。
